transcript.text: My Panasonic NN-ST45KWBPQ is sparking inside when I heat soup, little blue flashes on the right-hand wall and a crackling noise. I stopped it. Is it safe?

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Stop using the microwave now: switch it off at the socket and unplug it, and don't run it again (not even empty) until we know why it sparked. Never take the outer casing off — parts inside can hold a lethal charge even when it is unplugged. No, it is not safe to use. You must stop using the microwave immediately and leave it unplugged. The blue flashes on the right-hand wall and crackling noise are classic signs of arcing (sparking). 1. A metal object, foil, or a dish with a metallic rim was inside the oven.
2. The small flat cover panel on the side wall (the waveguide cover) has become burnt, holed, or carbonised from previous arcing. Do not try to run the appliance again to test if it clears. Even if you remove any metal items, a damaged internal cover panel will continue to spark and can damage the magnetron (the part that generates heat) or cause a fire. Please arrange for a qualified engineer to inspect and repair this. Do not attempt to open the casing yourself as there are lethal voltages stored in the capacitors even when unplugged.

claimsRejected.claim: Because you have already seen active sparking and stopped it, do not try to run the appliance again to test if it clears.

candidates: Metal or foil inside the cavity (medium)

reading.symptom: sparking inside, blue flashes on the right-hand wall, crackling noise

plan: They asked: "Is it safe?" - answer that first.

Safety: a microwave arcing hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Panasonic; model NN-ST45KWBPQ.
The fault they reported is: "sparking inside, blue flashes on the right-hand wall, crackling noise". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the safe checks that best tell those causes apart (most useful and simplest first, usually two to four), each with why it helps and what each result would mean; or, if one question would settle it sooner, ask that. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
